reproducibility_audit.decision: The existing paired artifacts isolate the first divergence before a new repeatability array is needed. Learned-method results are accepted as statistical rather than bit-exact reproductions.

findings: All 91 payload cells, including 84 trained adapters, passed receipt-bound artifact and log validation.

The same-seed replay broadly reproduced the prior seven-seed results. Final Acc@1 differences were 0.00 pp for frozen base, -0.25 pp for Q5, +3.11 pp for PIS, +1.07 pp for ReST-EM, +0.50 pp for STaR, -0.11 pp for TRICE-CV and -1.46 pp for RLOO.
Trajectory AUC was especially stable: the absolute replay difference was at most 0.62 pp for every source-mapped method.

The detailed same-seed audit found identical validation support throughout and exact frozen-base generations. For PIS, every seed had identical round-zero questions, sampled traces, trace order, posterior weights and objective before first diverging in the backward gradient or optimizer update.

For PIS seed 1231, the round-zero objective was exactly -76.1930935382843 in both runs, while the gradient norm differed by 0.066% (49.91465 versus 49.88194). Both tasks ran on seymour3 with the same H100, driver 550.127.08, CUDA 12.4, cuDNN 90100, PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124, Transformers 4.51.3 and PEFT 0.13.2.

Q5 round-zero sampled traces matched exactly, but BF16 log-probability scores differed before later sampling paths separated. This is consistent with GPU numerical variation being amplified by posterior weighting and repeated stochastic training.
Frozen-reader answer-guided Q5 reached 81.32% Final Acc@1, compared with 80.32% for its moving-reader control; the paired interval includes no effect.
Answer-guided PIS degraded to 63.64% Final Acc@1, while question-prompt PIS reached 80.00%.
limitations: This deliberately reuses the historical seeds and train-derived validation questions, so it is reproducibility evidence rather than fresh method-selection evidence.
Learned runs are not bit-exact; PIS has the largest endpoint replay difference despite nearly unchanged trajectory AUC.

The historical run used Python 3.11.15 and an earlier execution revision, while the replay used Python 3.11.0. Static review found no active scientific-path change for these cells, but the comparison cannot attribute every floating-point difference exclusively to CUDA.
The official GSM8K test split remained sealed.

studies.scientific_question: Does retaining 32 unique Q5 traces improve over support 16, and can a 16-draw posterior-sampled M-step retain that benefit at lower backward-pass cost?
findings: All 14 payload tasks, trained adapters, completion receipts and artifact hashes passed validation; no failure signature was present and the official GSM8K test was not used.
Full support 32 reached 81.86% Final Acc@1, 74.71% strict final accuracy and 80.20% trajectory AUC.

Against the paired support-16 Q5-MORE control, full support 32 improved Final Acc@1 by 0.96 pp with a paired 95% interval of [0.07, 1.82], and strict final accuracy by 0.89 pp [0.07, 1.71]. The extracted and strict AUC changes were smaller and their intervals included zero.

The 16-draw posterior-sampled M-step reached 81.32% Final Acc@1, 73.21% strict final accuracy and 80.21% trajectory AUC. Relative to full support it changed Final Acc@1 by -0.54 pp [-1.07, 0.04] and strict final accuracy by -1.50 pp [-2.21, -0.71].

Posterior sampling selected only 1.44 unique traces per question-step on average while covering 98.98% of posterior mass. It reduced mean backward tokens by 93.06% but reduced total accelerator-hours by only 6.15%, because generation and evaluation dominate wall-clock cost.
limitations: The historical support-16 control is reused rather than rerun because it has the same seven seeds and frozen protocol.
The fixed question schedule visits each optimization question once, so this tests within-question support depth rather than cross-round replay.
The same repeatedly used train-derived validation partition supports paired development evidence, not a fresh-question or official-test estimate.
The official GSM8K test split remains sealed.
next_actions: Treat support 32 with the full M-step as the strongest current Q5 support setting; preserve the uncertainty on trajectory AUC.
Do not replace the full M-step with plain posterior-categorical sampling: it collapses to roughly one or two unique traces and harms strict accuracy despite reducing backward tokens.
If M-step sampling is revisited, test a diversity-preserving constant-budget estimator such as posterior-stratified or without-replacement sampling rather than another categorical-draw count.
Use a fresh held-out or official-test confirmation only after the final method and stopping rule are frozen.

studies.scientific_question: Can deeper within-question candidate search improve Q5, and can an exact-top plus residual estimator preserve posterior-tail information more effectively than ordinary categorical M-step sampling?
limitations: The two support-32 controls are reused rather than rerun because they use the same seven seeds and frozen protocol.
The S64 cell doubles proposal draws while retaining four questions per round, so it tests within-question search depth rather than question breadth.
The exact-top plus residual estimator is unbiased conditional on the retained finite support; it does not correct Q5's answer-guided proposal mismatch.
The same repeatedly used train-derived validation partition supports paired development evidence, not a fresh-question or official-test estimate.
The official GSM8K test split remains sealed.
next_actions: Bind the prepared protocol to an immutable execution revision, deploy it to the AMN checkout and submit the held 14-task payload with its dependent validator.
After validation, compare S64 full support with S32 full support and compare exact-top residual sampling with both full support and ordinary categorical sampling.
Do not promote either intervention until all seven seeds, artifacts, logs, receipts and preregistered paired contrasts pass validation.

findings: Seven-seed means: Final Acc@1 77.46%, strict final accuracy 75.07%, normalized extracted-accuracy AUC 76.83%.
Paired Final Acc@1 gain versus same-seed frozen base is +1.29 pp, Student-t 95% interval [-1.47, +4.05]; strict gain is +17.57 pp [5.45, 29.69], positive on all seven seeds.

The clearest effect is improved output formatting; a held-out answer-accuracy gain is unresolved. Mean endpoint is below Q5, PIS, TRICE-CV and RLOO in the same-seed AMN replay controls. Trained-comparator gaps remain descriptive.
Per seed: 2048 training generations, 32 optimizer steps, 262778 generated training tokens, 412078 backward tokens and 0.684 H100-hours including recorded evaluation.

Verified seven receipts, 49 checkpoint-evaluation records, 224 training diagnostic records, all task terminals, full remote adapter hashes and a checksum-complete local non-adapter mirror. Same-seed optimization questions and demonstrations match the control panel. No official-test access.
